title: Alia Bhatt Didn't Join the Spy Universe — She's Here to Take It Over
excerpt: Alpha drops Thursday with a deadly assassin origin story, 75 million teaser views, and every A-lister watching. Here's why YRF's first female-led spy film might be the franchise's most dangerous entry yet.
body:
There's a moment in the Alpha teaser — you've probably already seen it, it hit 75 million views in 24 hours — where Alia Bhatt looks into the camera, bruised, cornered, and completely in control. She doesn't look like someone trying to prove she belongs in the YRF Spy Universe. She looks like someone who was always going to own it.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0

On July 3, that confidence gets a full two hours and twenty-one minutes to breathe. Alpha is the sixth film in Yash Raj Films' blockbuster spy franchise — the same universe that gave us Pathaan, War, and Tiger — but it's the first to put women at the centre. Not as love interests. Not as side missions. As the mission.

She Was Built to Kill

Alia plays a character forged in violence. Reports describe her role as a deadly assassin with an origin story darker than anything the Spy Universe has attempted — someone "raised and built to kill" from a young age. This isn't the wide-eyed girl from *Student of the Year* or even the fierce matriarch of *Gangubai Kathiawadi*. This is Alia in a register she's never attempted: gritty, physical, brutal. The kind of performance that's already drawing comparisons to Marvel's Black Widow — and those comparisons aren't coming from nobodies.

Shah Rukh Khan, SS Rajamouli, Priyanka Chopra, Salman Khan, Katrina Kaif, Jr NTR, and Vicky Kaushal all publicly praised the teaser within hours of its drop. When that list shows up for your launch, you're not releasing a film — you're dropping an event.

> "Reports describe her role as a deadly assassin with an origin story darker than anything the Spy Universe has attempted — someone "raised and built to kill" from a young age."

Alongside Alia is Sharvari Wagh, who's been on a quiet winning streak since *Bunny* and *Vedha*, and who reportedly has a role here that's anything but secondary. The two women are positioned as a formidable pair — think *Thelma & Louise* if Thelma knew twelve ways to kill you with a pen.

The Villain, the Legend, and the Worst-Kept Secret in Bollywood

![Spy Universe — Photo: Wikimedia Commons](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/d/d6/YRF_Spy_Universe_logo.jpg)

On the other side of the fight: Bobby Deol as the primary antagonist, leaning hard into the menacing energy he's been cultivating since *Animal*, and Anil Kapoor in a pivotal role that insiders say ties directly into the wider Spy Universe mythology. And then there's the cameo everyone's pretending not to know about: Hrithik Roshan reportedly makes an appearance, connecting Alpha to his *War* franchise in what should send spy-verse fans into cardiac arrest.

Director Shiv Rawail — who turned heads with the critically acclaimed *The Railway Men* on Netflix — is a deliberate choice. YRF didn't hand their first female spy film to a franchise veteran. They handed it to someone who's proven he can handle weight, ambiguity, and spectacle simultaneously.

> "Can't wait to watch the girls kick ass and give the boys a run for their money! This one is more than just a spy actioner.... it has way more than you expect or know." — Karan Johar, via Instagram

The Road to July 3

The journey here hasn't been smooth. Alpha was originally slated for Christmas 2025, then pushed to April 2026, then July 10, before YRF preponed it by a week to dodge the crush of Dhamaal 4 and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey later in the month. The delays were reportedly about perfecting the visual effects, and given that the teaser already looks like it cost more than most Hollywood mid-budgets, that gamble appears to have paid off.

Advance booking opened today with 700 tickets sold within hours across limited national chain showcasing, registering ₹2 lakh in pre-sales. YRF has issued strict exhibitor instructions: no screenings before 9:30 AM, ticket prices matched with *Welcome to the Jungle*, and minimum show allocations across multiplexes. It's a controlled, premium release — the kind you deploy when you believe your product can hold.

The competition is real. Akshay Kumar's Welcome to the Jungle is still commanding over 11,000 shows and has crossed the ₹100 crore mark. Alpha will need to carve out its own audience, and fast. But the franchise pedigree, the star power, and the sheer novelty of a female-led entry in India's biggest spy franchise suggest this is one fight Alia won't be walking away from.

For the diaspora: Alpha is getting a massive worldwide release across multiple languages. Whether you're catching it in Toronto, London, or San Jose, it's hitting a big screen near you.

Alpha releases in theatres worldwide on July 3, 2026. Advance booking is open now.
